title: How much sunlight does a leaf turn into food?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: What happens to the sunlight a leaf does not use?
Are leaves better than solar panels?

explain.say: Leaves are solar panels, but not very efficient ones. Here is a rough energy budget for a sunny leaf, showing where 100 units of sunlight end up.

draw.text: How much sunlight does a leaf turn into food?

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: inside a leaf. Look at the cuticle, the upper epidermis and the palisade cells. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: How much sunlight does a leaf turn into food?

explain.say: Only about 1 or 2 units end up stored as sugar. That small share feeds almost every living thing on Earth, from the plant itself to the animals that eat it.
A big share is reflected or passes straight through, including much of the green light and the invisible infrared. Chlorophyll can only use certain colours.
Most of the light the leaf does absorb turns into heat. Much of that heat evaporates water from the leaf, which cools it, just as sweat cools your skin.

faq.a: Most crops store only about 1 percent of the sunlight that falls on them as chemical energy, and very fast-growing ones about 2 percent. The best possible is thought to be around 4 to 6 percent.
asks: What percent of sunlight do plants use?

faq.a: Chlorophyll uses only part of the sunlight, mostly red and blue. Some energy is lost as heat in each chemical step, and plants also spend energy on respiration.
asks: Why do plants waste so much sunlight?

faq.q: Are solar panels better than leaves?
faq.a: At turning light into energy, yes: common solar panels convert about 20 percent of sunlight into electricity. But leaves build, repair and copy themselves, and store their energy as food.

faq.q: Why do leaves not overheat in the sun?
faq.a: Water evaporating from the stomata carries heat away, cooling the leaf. Leaves also lose heat to the air around them, and some turn edge-on to very strong sun.

faq.q: If plants use so little sunlight, how do they feed the world?
faq.a: Sunlight brings an enormous amount of energy, and plants cover huge areas of land and ocean. Even 1 percent of all that is enough to feed almost all life on Earth.

facts: Most crops convert about 1 percent of the sunlight that falls on them into stored chemical energy.
The maximum possible efficiency of photosynthesis has been estimated at about 4.6 percent for plants like wheat and 6 percent for plants like maize.
Common silicon solar panels convert around 20 percent of sunlight into electricity.
